title: At the food stall: ordering and saying how good it is
title_target: ຢູ່ຮ້ານອາຫານ — Yùu hâan aa-hǎan
goal: Order food and drinks, ask for something added or left out, praise the taste, and ask for the bill — one sitting that covers the whole business of eating out.
bekal: order with ເອົາ and ຂໍ
ໃສ່ and ບໍ່ໃສ່ for ingredients put in

ຫິວ and ອີ່ມ for hungry and full

dialogs.title: ບົດສົນທະນາ — A roadside feu stall, seven in the morning
dialogs.intro: Budi is having breakfast with Bounmy. Notice that ordering in Laos almost never takes a long sentence — the dish, the number, the classifier, done.

lines.speaker: ແມ່ຄ້າ:
lines.text: [ສະບາຍດີ|Sa-baai-dii] [ເອົາ|Ao][ຫຍັງ|nyǎng]

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ເອົາ|Ao][ເຝີ|fǒe][ໄກ່|kài][ສອງ|sǎwng][ຖ້ວຍ|thûay][ເດີ້|dòe]
lines.id: Two bowls of chicken feu, please.

lines.speaker: ແມ່ຄ້າ:
lines.text: [ໃສ່|Sài][ຜັກ|phák][ບໍ່|bàw] [ເຜັດ|Phét][ບໍ່|bàw]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ໃສ່|Sài][ຜັກ|phák] [ແຕ່|Tèe][ບໍ່|bàw][ໃສ່|sài][ຜັກຫອມ|phák-hǎwm][ເດີ້|dòe] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ບໍ່|bàw][ມັກ|mak]
lines.id: With vegetables, but no cilantro, please. I don't like it.
lines.literal: put-in — vegetable. but — not — put-in — fragrant-leaf — (friendly). I — not — like.

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ເຜັດ|Phét][ໜ້ອຍ|nàwy][ໜຶ່ງ|nʉ̀ng] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ກິນ|kin][ເຜັດ|phét][ໄດ້|dâi][ແຕ່|tèe][ບໍ່|bàw][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai]
lines.id: A little spicy. I can eat spicy food, but not a lot.
lines.literal: spicy — little — one. I — eat — spicy — can — but — not — much.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ຂໍ|Khǎw][ນ້ຳ|nâm][ສອງ|sǎwng][ແກ້ວ|kêeo][ນຳ|nám][ແດ່|dèe]
lines.id: Two glasses of water too, please.
lines.literal: ask-for — water — two — glass — along — a-bit.

lines.speaker: ແມ່ຄ້າ:
lines.text: [ໄດ້|Dâi][ເລີຍ|lóei] [ຖ້າ|Thàa][ໜ້ອຍ|nàwy][ໜຶ່ງ|nʉ̀ng][ເດີ້|dòe]

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ແຊບ|Sèep][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai][ເນາະ|nāw] [ຮ້ານ|Hâan][ນີ້|nîi][ດີ|dii]
lines.id: Really delicious, isn't it? This place is good.
lines.literal: delicious — much — isn't-it? shop — this — good.

lines.speaker: ບຸນມີ:
lines.text: [ແມ່ນ|Mèen][ແລ້ວ|lèeo] [ຂ້ອຍ|Khàwy][ມາ|maa][ກິນ|kin][ທຸກ|thuk][ເຊົ້າ|sâo] [ອີ່ມ|Ìm][ບໍ່|bàw]
lines.id: Yes. I eat here every morning. Are you full?
lines.literal: right — already. I — come — eat — every — morning. full — (question)?

lines.speaker: ບູດີ:
lines.text: [ອີ່ມ|Ìm][ຫຼາຍ|lǎai] [ຄິດ|Khit][ເງິນ|ngóen][ແດ່|dèe]

lines.speaker: ແມ່ຄ້າ:
lines.text: [ສາມ|Sǎam][ສິບ|síp][ພັນ|phán][ກີບ|kìip][ເຈົ້າ|jâo]

notes: **ເອົາ ao to order, ຂໍ khǎw to ask.** Both are fine at a stall, but they feel different: *ເອົາເຝີສອງຖ້ວຍ* is an order, *ຂໍນ້ຳແດ່* is a request. For something free or small — plain water, a spoon, tissues — use *ຂໍ*.

**ໃສ່ sài means "to put in" and is the key word for everything food-related.** *ໃສ່ຜັກ* (with vegetables), *ບໍ່ໃສ່ນ້ຳຕານ* (no sugar), *ໃສ່ນ້ຳກ້ອນ* (with ice). The same word means "to wear" for clothes: *ໃສ່ເສື້ອ* (put on a shirt).

**ເຜັດບໍ່ phét bàw is a question you WILL hear.** A safe answer for most visitors: *ເຜັດໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ* (a little spicy). If you really can't handle heat, say *ບໍ່ເຜັດ* — but be ready, because "not spicy" in Laos can still feel warm.

**ແຊບ sèep is the word for "delicious," and it's not the Thai *อร่อย*.** It's one of the most typically Lao words — also used in Isan, northeastern Thailand. Saying it at a stall is guaranteed to make the owner smile. Stronger forms: *ແຊບຫຼາຍ* (really delicious) and *ແຊບອີ່ຫຼີ sèep ìi-lǐi* (seriously delicious).
**ຫິວ hǐu = hungry, ອີ່ມ ìm = full.** Both are adjectives, so no verb is needed: *ຂ້ອຍຫິວ* (I'm hungry). For thirsty, Lao says "hungry for water": *ຫິວນ້ຳ hǐu nâm*.

**ຄິດເງິນແດ່ khit ngóen dèe = "the bill, please," literally "count the money, please."** Small stalls have no receipts; the owner adds it up in their head and tells you the amount. You pay at the table, not at a register.
**ທຸກ thuk = "every."** *ທຸກເຊົ້າ* (every morning), *ທຸກມື້* (every day), *ທຸກຄົນ* (everyone). It goes in front of the noun and needs no classifier.

**ຖ້າ thàa has twins you need to keep apart.** *ຖ້າ thàa* with a low falling tone means **"to wait"** (*ຖ້າໜ້ອຍໜຶ່ງ* = wait a moment), while the *ຖ້າ* you learned in Unit 3 means **"if."** The spelling is the same; context separates them — and luckily they rarely appear in the same sentence.
**ເຈົ້າ jâo at the end of a seller's sentence is a polite "yes,"** not "you." Sellers often close their sentences with it as a sign of respect for the customer.

grammars.title: Ordering: one pattern, every dish
body: A Lao order can always be built from this frame. Not a single linking word is required.

ກາເຟຮ້ອນ *kaa-fée hâwn*

after: To change an order, attach *ໃສ່* or *ບໍ່ໃສ່* at the end: *ເອົາເຝີໄກ່ ບໍ່ໃສ່ຜັກຫອມ* (chicken feu, no cilantro).

grammars.title: Tastes and cooking methods
after: Taste adjectives are complete sentences on their own: *ແຊບ* already means "it's delicious." To negate, put *ບໍ່* in front: *ບໍ່ເຜັດ* (not spicy).

sections.title: Food you'll really come across in Laos

head: Lao
Say it
What it is
rows: sticky rice — the staple, eaten by hand
beef/chicken noodle soup, the national breakfast
papaya salad (the Lao som tam), usually very spicy
spiced minced meat — the national dish of Laos
baguette — a French legacy, filled with meat and vegetables

blocks.text: One thing to know before eating with Lao people: **sticky rice is eaten with the right hand**, squeezed into a small ball and dipped into the dishes. Its woven basket — *ຕິບເຂົ້າ típ khào* — is opened to mark the start of the meal and closed again when you're done. Closing it signals that you're full, more clearly than words.

Notice the prefix **ໝາກ *màak*** in front of almost every fruit name: *ໝາກກ້ວຍ* (banana), *ໝາກນາວ* (lime), *ໝາກຫຸ່ງ* (papaya), *ໝາກໄມ້* (fruit). If you hear *màak-* at the start of a word, it's almost certainly about fruit.

blocks.text: The sentence *ຂ້ອຍກິນຊີ້ນໝູບໍ່ໄດ້* matters if you avoid pork, whether for religious or other reasons. Pork appears in many Lao dishes, often as a broth you can't see. An even safer sentence: *ຂ້ອຍກິນໄດ້ແຕ່ໄກ່ກັບປາ khàwy kin dâi tèe kài kap paa* — "I can only eat chicken and fish."
